Subject: RE: Unexpected latency and 5xx spike affecting production

Nikhil —

We started seeing a sharp latency increase and a corresponding spike in 500/503 errors on our Primex storefront between 08:45–09:05 PDT. Traffic is normal; no config changes on our side. Impact: user requests timing out (our front-end shows >2s extra on average) and a 4.1% error rate on checkout endpoints.

Attached: primex_error_log.zip (logs + small sample request traces). Our SRE (sre@primex.com) is available — we need a short war-room and a concrete mitigation plan. We are seeing revenue impact right now.

Please advise ETA on triage.

—
Aisha Malik

Adding quick triage notes ahead of the call:
- Primex appears to have a sudden shift in sequence length distribution (more long-context requests) which could be causing KV cache pressure and increased cache misses.
- Early-metrics (preliminary): 95th p50 -> 400ms to ~950ms; tail p99 up to 3.6s.

I've started a shared War-room doc and uploaded a KPI snapshot (primex_kpi_snapshot.csv). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/primex-warroom

On the call we'll: confirm root cause hypothesis, propose immediate mitigations (scale pool + conservative quantization/shorter context), and draft customer-facing status text.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@primex.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:02:37 -07:00
Subject: Re: Primex incident — preliminary findings

On the triage: we've confirmed elevated KV cache miss rates correlated with the error spike. Memory pressure on serving racks increased when several long-context jobs concurrently hit the model.

Immediate actions taken (10:00–10:18 PDT):
- Scaled Primex's dedicated pool from 6->10 instances (temporary burst).
- Enabled conservative batching cap (max batch size reduced) to lower per-request queueing.
- Throttled a small subset of long-context background jobs (with Primex SRE approval).

Prelim metrics post-mitigation: median latency down ~180ms, p99 reduced from 3.6s -> ~1.1s, error rate down to 0.9% (still above baseline). See attached latency_trace.png.

Next steps: run a longer 60-minute observation window; if stable, we'll work on a persistent runbook: cache-sizing recommendation, more granular routing by sequence-length, and model quantization profile adjustments.

—Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: latency_trace.png
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:05:49 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief: Primex production latency + temporary capacity request

Team — quick exec summary and ask:
- Incident: Primex production experienced a latency and 5xx spike from ~08:45–09:05 PDT; impact to revenue (checkout failures).
- Root cause (prelim): burst of long-context requests causing KV cache thrash and memory pressure on their dedicated serving pool.
- Mitigation completed: temporary pool scale-up and batching cap; p99 improved to ~1.1s and error rate reduced to <1%.

Ask: approval to keep temporary burst (10 instances) for 24 hours while we implement longer-term tuning (cache-sizing + route-by-sequence-length). If leadership OKs, we'll absorb the initial cost for the burst and propose a formal credits/discount conversation with Primex for the interruption.

If approved, I'll notify Primex with an expected timeline and the runbook we discussed.

Thanks,
Nikhil
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@primex.com>, Primex SRE <sre@primex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Primex incident update — mitigation in place, next steps

Aisha / Primex SRE — follow-up after today's triage:

Summary:
- Root cause (confirmed): KV cache saturation caused by an unusual surge of long-context requests; cache misses caused backend queueing and 5xx errors.
- Immediate mitigation: temporary Dedicated pool increase (6->10 instances) and conservative batching cap. These actions lowered p99 and reduced 5xx rate to <1%.

Attachments & runbook:
- Attached runbook: primex_runbook_v1.md (short-term ops steps, rollback plan, monitoring thresholds).
- Links: War-room doc + KPI snapshots: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/primex-warroom

Next steps / timeline:
- 24-hr observation window (we recommend keeping burst capacity for that period).
- Engineering to deliver cache-sizing and route-by-length changes in a staged rollout this week (ETA: 72 hours).
- We'll schedule a post-mortem and a customer-facing RCA once the longer-term change set is validated.

If you approve keeping the temporary burst, we'll keep it active and absorb the cost for 24 hours; after that we'll propose a commercial adjustment. Happy to jump on another call if you want additional detail.

Best regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachments: primex_runbook_v1.md
